topic: Powers of i and the complex plane
subtitle: Reading powers of the imaginary unit and points on the complex plane

problems.desc: Rubric for the plotted points. Three points must appear on the grid and be labelled: the given number at two right and five up, its negative at two left and five down, and the doubled number at four right and ten up. Full credit needs the negative shown as the reflection of the given point through the origin and the double shown on the same ray from the origin, twice as far out. Grade the plotting against the values the student wrote above, so a correct plot of a wrong pair still earns the plotting mark.

Rubric for the plot and the written description. The grid must show the given number at three right and one up and the product at one left and three up. The description must say that multiplying by the imaginary unit turns the point a quarter turn, ninety degrees, counterclockwise about the origin, and that the distance from the origin does not change. Accept a quarter turn described as a rotation without the word degrees. No credit for describing only the sign changes without naming a turn about the origin.

traps.desc: reduced the exponents modulo 4 but read a remainder of 2 as +1 instead of -1

problems.desc: Rubric for the plotted point. One point must be marked four units left of the origin and three units up, on the grid provided, and the segment joining it to the origin may be drawn. Credit the plot if it matches the number the student wrote in the first blank, so plotting is graded separately from converting the words into standard form.

Rubric for the written explanation. A full-credit answer says that multiplying by the imaginary unit turns a point a quarter turn about the origin, so doing it twice is a half turn of one hundred eighty degrees, which sends every point to the opposite side of the origin and therefore negates both parts. Accept wording built on two quarter turns making a half turn. No credit for only stating that i squared equals negative one without connecting it to the turn.

Rubric for the plot and the written justification. The grid must show the starting point at five right and two up and the finishing point at two right and five down. The justification must say that each quarter turn is one multiplication by the imaginary unit, so three quarter turns in a row is multiplication by the imaginary unit three times, which is the cube of the imaginary unit. Accept an answer that adds that three quarter turns counterclockwise is the same as one quarter turn clockwise. No credit for arithmetic alone with no statement linking repeated turning to the repeated factor.
